newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO sees return of momentum.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO sees return of momentum.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton said Friday the second quarter was very difficult but the automaker intends to regain momentum with the help of several new products this year.

"Our momentum appears to be re-building -- we had our best June ever for light truck sales," Eaton said in a statement. "Looking ahead, we're very enthusiastic about the new products that we will launch in the third quarter, including the Dodge Durango, Chrysler Concorde and Dodge Intrepid."
Chrysler today reported second quarter earnings that were cut dramatically from a year earlier by a 29-day strike at an engine plant by the United Auto Workers union.
"The second quarter was a very difficult one for Chrysler. Our results were significantly affected by the UAW strike -- our vehicle shipments were reduced by an estimated 89,000 units," Eaton said.
Chrysler said the strike at its Mound Road plant in Detroit cost it $438 million, or $0.64 a share.

Chrysler's incentives increased to an average of $980 per vehicle during the quarter, from $625 in the year-ago period. Chrysler finished the second quarter with incentives of $1,195 per vehicle, indicating that spending to lure customers was continuing to increase.
Eaton said the U.S. car and truck market "has become significantly more competitive than we expected earlier in the year."

He said Chrysler had stepped up its efforts to eliminate waste and reduce expenses. Those steps include a temporary freeze on outside hiring, reducing overtime and travel, and delaying some discretionary capital spending projects.
A Chrysler spokesman said the capital spending reductions will not affect any of the automaker's future car and truck programs.
